CHAPTER I

The morning came in slowly over the roofs, and the whole street waited for
it the way a room waits for someone who has said that they will arrive. A
cart went past and did not stop. Somewhere below, a door was opened and
then, after a moment's thought, closed again.

He counted the panes in the window twice and got a different answer each
time, which told him something about the morning and nothing at all about
the window. It was the kind of arithmetic that only works before breakfast.

CHAPTER II

Later there would be work, and the particular relief of it, which is that
work asks nothing of you except that you do it. Until then there was the
chair by the window, and the light coming up, and no reason to move.
